title: Two Orbits
statement:
Let $O$ be a point in the plane. Point $A$ moves at constant speed around the circle with centre $O$ and radius $16$ metres, completing one revolution every $20$ seconds. Point $B$ moves at constant speed around the circle with centre $O$ and radius $39$ metres, completing one revolution every $30$ seconds, in the same rotational sense as $A$.

Let $D$ be the closed disc with centre $O$ and radius $r$ metres, where $0 < r < 16$. As the points move, the segment $AB$ sometimes has at least one point in common with $D$. Each maximal continuous time interval during which this holds lasts exactly $20$ seconds.

The value of $r$ can be written as $\frac{a\sqrt{b}}{c}$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are positive integers, $a$ and $c$ are coprime, and $b$ is not divisible by the square of any prime. Find $a + b + c$.
hints: Whether the segment $AB$ meets the disc depends only on the size of angle $AOB$, not on the actual positions of $A$ and $B$. Think about how this angle changes over time.

Use relative angular speed. $A$ turns at $18^\circ$ per second and $B$ at $12^\circ$ per second, so the directed angle from $B$ to $A$ grows at a steady $6^\circ$ per second, and a $20$-second interval sweeps out $120^\circ$.

Contact is centred on the moment when $O$ lies between $A$ and $B$, where angle $AOB$ is $180^\circ$. So contact starts and ends when angle $AOB$ is $120^\circ$ and $AB$ is tangent to the disc. Then $r$ is the altitude from $O$ in the triangle with sides $16$ and $39$ enclosing $120^\circ$, which you can find using the cosine rule and the area.
solution:
Let $\theta\in[0^\circ,180^\circ]$ be the angle $AOB$ and $d(\theta)$ the distance from $O$ to segment $AB$. Contact happens iff $d\le r$.

Put $u=\cos\theta$. Then $AB^2=1777-1248u>0$. The angle at $B$ is acute because $OB>OA$. The angle at $A$ is non-acute iff $OA^2+AB^2\le OB^2$, i.e. $u\ge \frac{16}{39}$. In that case the nearest point is $A$, so $d=16>r$ and there is no contact.

For $u<\frac{16}{39}$ the foot of the perpendicular lies on the segment, so $d$ is the altitude from $O$. Comparing areas, $AB\cdot d=624\sin\theta$, so
$$d^2=\dfrac{624^2(1-u^2)}{1777-1248u}.$$
For $g(u)=\frac{1-u^2}{1777-1248u}$, the numerator of $g'(u)$ is
$$1248u^2-3554u+1248=2(16u-39)(39u-16),$$
which is positive for $u<\frac{16}{39}$. So $d$ is strictly decreasing in $\theta$ there, continuously from $16$ to $0$ at $\theta=180^\circ$. Hence there is a unique $\theta_0$ with $d(\theta_0)=r$, and contact holds exactly when $\theta\ge\theta_0$.

The directed angle from $B$ to $A$ increases at $18^\circ-12^\circ=6^\circ$ per second. Contact holds while it lies in $[\theta_0,360^\circ-\theta_0]$ modulo $360^\circ$, an interval of length $\frac{360^\circ-2\theta_0}{6^\circ}$ seconds. Setting this equal to $20$ gives $\theta_0=120^\circ$. Here $\cos120^\circ=-\frac{1}{2}<\frac{16}{39}$, so this is valid.

At $\theta=120^\circ$, $AB^2=256+1521+624=2401$, so $AB=49$. Then
$$r=\dfrac{16\cdot 39\sin120^\circ}{49}=\dfrac{312\sqrt3}{49}\approx 11.03,$$
which lies in $(0,16)$. Since $312=2^3\cdot3\cdot13$ is coprime to $49$ and $3$ is squarefree, $a=312$, $b=3$, $c=49$, and $a+b+c=364$.

solution_figures.alt: Two concentric circles with centre O and radii 16 and 39, the outer one shown as an arc, with A on the inner circle and B on the outer. At the moment contact begins, angle AOB is 120 degrees and AB = 49. Segment AB just touches the disc of radius r around O, at the foot F of the perpendicular from O, with a right angle at F.
